extracted.intended_audience: Commissioner of Indian Affairs / Department of the Interior and Indian agency officials
extracted.subtask_description: An 1880 United States Indian agent annual report describing tribal conditions, education, land and fund management, and recommendations for administrative and legislative action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Education funding and expenditure
rubrics_metrics.description: The nation expended [specified sums] for educational purposes (examples: Cherokees $60,803.69; Choctaws $31,700 plus $4,200 for students sent to college; Chickasaws $58,000; Creeks $28,356; Seminoles $7,500).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and report amounts spent annually for education; use funds for common schools, seminaries, boarding schools, and sending students to States; ensure an education fund is established and appropriations are recorded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of teacher pay and school supplies
rubrics_metrics.description: Teachers are paid and books furnished from the school fund of the nation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure teacher salaries and instructional materials are paid out of designated school funds; document average teacher salary levels (e.g., common school teachers average $500 per annum; some receive $450 per annum).

rubrics_metrics.name: School-house construction and maintenance by community
rubrics_metrics.description: The school-house is built and kept in repair by the neighborhood in which the school-house is located.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local communities should be responsible for building and maintaining school-houses; report condition and occupancy of school buildings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence and operation of seminaries and boarding schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of male/female seminaries and boarding schools with stated attendance numbers (examples: male seminary 89, female seminary 85; Pottawatomie Industrial Boarding School—buildings and farm described).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document seminary/boarding-school capacity, attendance, facilities, farm support, and industrial training components; report whether buildings are adequate or need repair.

rubrics_metrics.name: Orphan asylum provisioning
rubrics_metrics.description: Orphan asylums whose inmates are clothed, fed, and educated by the nation from a fund set apart for that purpose (example: Cherokee orphan asylum with 120 inmates).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain a dedicated fund to fully provide for orphans' clothing, food, and education; report inmate numbers and services provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contracting schools and terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain schools are let by contract for five years; contractors supply everything except clothing (or supply everything in some asylums).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use multi-year contracts to operate schools; specify contractor responsibilities (supplies, management), and note exceptions (e.g., clothing supplied by nation for pupils).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for out-of-state education
rubrics_metrics.description: Nations may appropriate funds to send boys and girls to the States to be educated at the nation's expense (examples: Choctaws sent 22 students; Chickasaws educated 15 boys and girls in the States).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report number and cost of students sent out-of-state; justify selections and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status determination and treatment of citizenship claimants
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimants to citizenship who have applied to citizenship court and been rejected (or pending review) are deprived of privileges; agent investigates and permits them to remain if prima facie just claim exists; long delays are detrimental.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate claimants per Department rules; permit those with prima facie claims to remain pending final determination; recommend timely settlement of citizenship claims to avoid harm to nation and claimants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define legal status for former slaves/residents (freedmen)
rubrics_metrics.description: More than 3,000 negroes (former slaves) among Choctaws have no school privileges except limited U.S. government support; 'Some measures should be adopted to define the status of these people, so that the Indian, as well as the negro, could have the benefit of law.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt measures/legislation to define the legal status of freedmen on tribal lands to ensure equal access to law and educational benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement against intruders and trespassers
rubrics_metrics.description: There are a large number of intruders among the Chickasaws (and others); under new government they may be compelled to seek a more congenial climate; whites trespassing and stealing horses were arrested and punished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce treaty and reservation boundaries; arrest and prosecute trespassers; report incidents and enforcement actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of unused government property
rubrics_metrics.description: The government owns an agency building with no further use; 'the building should be appraised and sold; should it be abandoned it would soon go to ruin.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appraise and sell government buildings not in use; consider current occupancy and maintenance needs before disposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agricultural assistance and resident farming instruction
rubrics_metrics.description: Appointment of a farmer/superintendent for Indians is productive and needed because 'the Indian is so unused to the cultivation of the soil'—a resident farmer directing and assisting with work would yield favorable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide resident farmers/superintendents, implements, tools, and seeds; teach husbandry and assign supervised farm work to both children and adults to increase yields and long-term agricultural adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate land use and improvement
rubrics_metrics.description: Reserve lands vary in suitability—some are well adapted for farming; other tracts 'not suitable for farming purposes present excellent opportunities for grazing.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess land for suitability and plan use accordingly (cultivation where appropriate; grazing where cultivation is poor); encourage planting of shade and fruit trees and construction of permanent improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investment and management of tribal funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Tribal funds include school funds, improvement funds, general funds temporarily invested; tribes desire to fund improve­ment funds (example: increase improvement fund from $17,900 to $60,000) and support shops (wagon-shop).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest and fund tribal improvement funds and productive enterprises; seek legislative authorization when needed; report desire for Congressional action (e.g., Senate bill No. 1505).

rubrics_metrics.name: Blacksmith and trade shop standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Blacksmith shop supported by $1,009 per annum; a superior mechanic should be employed who is proficient in iron and wood work; shop conducted on same principle as those in white farming communities; apprentice employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fund and staff trade shops with skilled mechanics; require quality workmanship; use shops as vocational training for apprentices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allottee rights, estate settlement, and minority transitions
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no provision for settlement of estates of deceased allottees nor for minors who attain majority to become citizens; complications demand legislation: 1. Appraisement and sale of lands of removed allottees; 2. Settlement of estates of deceased allottees not citizens; 3. Grant privileges to allottees who were minors and have attained majority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommend legislation to create probate/estate settlement procedures and to enfranchise or otherwise provide for allottees who reach majority; address protection of allotted lands from depredation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of unused reserved mill-site and missionary lands
rubrics_metrics.description: Article reserved mill-site and missionary lands outside reserve limits have been unused; timber sold/stolen; recommend that these reservations be sold and interest applied to agricultural and pastoral promotion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reserved lands are not used for intended public purpose, consider selling and applying proceeds to tribal development (with appropriate safeguards).

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial education model in boarding schools
rubrics_metrics.description: At industrial/boarding schools, pupils perform daily chores: boys assist on the farm and with stock; girls assist in laundry, kitchen, and clothing work; children are taught to labor before and after school hours to cultivate industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine academic instruction with supervised industrial labor to inculcate habits of industry and practical skills; document assignments and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of timber and recovery of stray/stolen stock
rubrics_metrics.description: Timber standing on reserves has been fully protected; horses and ponies that strayed or were stolen have been recovered at slight expense borne by the Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure protection of natural resources and implement measures to recover stolen animals with minimal cost to tribes; report results of protection efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing harmful sales/leases to white settlers
rubrics_metrics.description: Allotments sold or leased to white persons in violation of treaties; chiefs authorized or encouraged such sales, causing injury to Indians.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage and prevent unauthorized sales/leases to non-Indians; inform and educate chiefs and members about illegality and consequences; protect tribal lands from exploitative transactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of thrift and use of annuities for permanent improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Instead of frittering annuities on transient items, one-third or more is used to purchase lumber and articles that conduce to comfort, health, and happiness; recommendation that annuity expenditures be directed to improvements and make titles inalienable to promote thrift.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage saving and spending annuities on durable improvements (houses, lumber, implements); consider legal measures such as inalienability of land to protect investments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting on demographic and health statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: Annual reporting of population, births, deaths, sickness (examples: tribe numbers, births and deaths counts, absentees), and absentees' locations and occupations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed demographic statistics in annual reports (population by sex, births, deaths, absentees and where located) to inform policy and resource allocation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Housing construction and community improvements
rubrics_metrics.description: Indians built substantial houses (log, frame, rock house 24x32 divided in six rooms); planted shade and fruit trees; improvements purchased with their money.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support and report on construction of substantial dwellings and community improvements; encourage use of annuities/improvement funds for long-term infrastructure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match education and employment opportunities to local economy
rubrics_metrics.description: Indians find remunerative wages in lumbering, mines, and mill work; many adapt to occupations such as piling lumber and loading vessels; agriculture is advanced where land permits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote vocational opportunities that fit local economic activities; document employment types and recommend vocational training aligned with local industries.
